title: The Existence of Diagonal Quantum Latin Squares with Maximum Cardinality
summary: A quantum Latin square of order \(n\), denoted by \(\operatorname{QLS}(n)\), is an \(n \times n\) square whose entries are unit column vectors in the \(n\)-dimensional Hilbert space \(\mathcal{H}_n\), such that each row and each column forms an orthonormal basis of \(\mathcal{H}_n\). The cardinality of a QLS($n$) is the number of distinct vectors up to a global phase in the array. A \(\mathrm{QLS}(n)\) whose main diagonal and anti-diagonal each forms an orthonormal basis of \(\mathcal{H}_n\) is called a diagonal quantum Latin square (\(\mathrm{DQLS}(n)\)).
